# Related Work

The RI problem can be seen as essentially a missing data problem [@ehrhardt2021rejectReview],
and therefore is related to matters as sample selection, data representability and
their consequences in estimation of classifiers, decision functions and evaluation.
The review of @ehrhardt2021rejectReview revealed many structural problems in
existing RI-methods and just like @HandHanley1993CanRIWork it concludes that for
RI to be possible it is necessary to make strong assumptions or include external
information like a labeled sample of a typical reject region. Furthermore, in a
spirit close to @ehrhardt2021rejectReview, I believe that being explicit about
the assumptions both on the data generating process studied, and the methodology
help to rigorously assess the feasibility, potential, limitations and possible
application fields of an RI approach.

This being considered, this literature review considers the following questions

1. How and why does the RI-approach work? Which assumptions are necessary and which
   aspect is exploited to do RI.
2. Do the authors discuss their assumptions explicitly and put them in relation to
   practical and theoretical considerations?
3. How do the authors asses their own work?
4. Is the inherent dynamic feedback nature of the acceptance bias considered?

All of this information is summarized in table @tbl-lit-review in the appendix.
First is clear that assumptions on the DGP and the methodology are often ignored, which
from my read also relates to a weaker discussion of the assessment of the goodness
and practicality of the model. Second, papers using more information than only
cross-sectional features and the labels of the accepts tend to also conclude having
better performance. Finally, no paper has been found that has formulated the RI problem
from a dynamic perspective nor has it been researched whether this perspective can
be used to obtain important learning signals.
